rope.title: Yellow Line - No Parking - Rope DIY
rope.diy_instruction: Find yellow shoelace, old rope, or yellow plastic strip. Tie one end to your bedroom door handle. Let it hang like a yellow line on road. Every time you enter room, touch it and say 'Yellow line = NO parking ANY time'. Leave for 7 days.
rope.why: Embodied cognition: Touching physical rope creates sensorimotor memory. Kontra 2015 shows 40% better recall vs reading. Yellow line abstract rule becomes physical boundary.
rope.materials: Yellow shoelace / string / plastic, door handle, 0 cost
rope.time: 2 mins to make, 7 days bedroom poster effect

stop.title: STOP Sign 3 Second Rule - Paper Clock
stop.diy_instruction: Take A4 paper, write STOP big in red koki, write '3 SEC' above. Stick on wall above bed. Every morning, look at it and count '1 thousand, 2 thousand, 3 thousand' out loud. This is K53 stop rule.
stop.why: Spaced repetition + visual cue in bedroom = habit formation. Morning routine anchors memory. 3 sec rule prevents rolling stop fines.
stop.materials: A4 paper, red koki, Prestik, 0 cost

colour.title: Road Sign Colours - 3 Circles
colour.diy_instruction: Draw 3 circles on A4. Colour first red, second yellow with black border, third blue with white inside. Write under: Red=STOP/Prohibition, Yellow=WARNING, Blue=INFO. Stick on cupboard.
colour.why: Color coding: Red prohibition, yellow warning, blue info is universal K53 pattern. Drawing activates visual memory vs reading.
colour.materials: A4, red yellow blue kokis, 0 cost

mirror.title: Blind Spot Check - Mirror Paper
mirror.diy_instruction: Take small paper, write 'CARS? PEOPLE? BEHIND?' Stick on bathroom mirror. Every time you look in mirror, turn head left and right like checking blind spot. Say 'Check blind spot'.
mirror.why: Habit stacking: Existing mirror habit + new blind spot check. Physical head turn creates motor memory. Prevents accidents.

speed.title: Speed Limits - Shoelace Knots
speed.diy_instruction: Take shoelace. Make 1 knot = 60km/h town, 2 knots close together = 100km/h single road, 3 knots = 120km/h freeway. Keep lace in pocket. Touch knots before answering speed Q.
speed.why: Tactile memory: Knots encode numbers. Touching while answering = retrieval cue. No need to memorize numbers abstractly.
